title: How Do Video Foundation Models Encode Intuitive Physics? Probing Across Pretraining Paradigms
abstract: arXiv:2606.09646v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study whether pretrained video foundation models encode intuitive-physics information in their frozen representations, and how this information varies across model families, layers, and probe types. Using frozen-feature probing on IntPhys2 and Minimal Video Pairs (MVP), we compare predictive joint-embedding models (V-JEPA), masked reconstruction models (VideoMAE), and a diffusion-based video generator (LTX-Video). V-JEPA achieves the strongest overall results across benchmarks, especially with probes that model temporal dynamics, while VideoMAE remains competitive and LTX-Video recovers weaker but non-trivial signal. translated_title: 视频基础模型如何编码直觉物理？跨预训练范式的探测研究
translated_abstract: 我们研究预训练的视频基础模型是否在其冻结表示中编码了直觉物理信息，以及这些信息在不同模型家族、网络层和探测方法之间如何变化。通过在IntPhys2和Minimal Video Pairs（MVP）数据集上进行冻结特征探测，我们比较了预测式联合嵌入模型（V-JEPA）、掩码重建模型（VideoMAE）以及基于扩散的视频生成模型（LTX-Video）。V-JEPA在所有基准测试中取得了最强的整体结果，尤其是在采用建模时间动态的探测器时表现突出；VideoMAE仍保持竞争力，而LTX-Video则能恢复出较弱但非平凡的信号。逐层分析表明，物理相关信息在早期层中最弱，并在中后层深度时最易获取；时间控制实验表明，打乱帧序会显著降低性能，尤其是在MVP数据集上。总之，这些结果表明直觉物理知识
tldr: 本研究通过冻结特征探测发现，不同预训练范式的视频基础模型编码直觉物理信息的能力存在显著差异，其中V-JEPA表现最佳，且物理相关知识在中后网络层最为丰富、高度依赖正确的帧序。
en_tdlr: Frozen-feature probing reveals that intuitive-physics encoding in video foundation models varies significantly across pretraining paradigms, with V-JEPA performing best, physics knowledge most accessible at intermediate-to-late layers, and strong dependence on correct frame ordering.
